units.intent: A Bedrock plugin implementing a simple named-blob cache backed by a `cache` SQLite table with a trigger-maintained running size, paired with an in-memory LRU tracker used to decide what to evict, exposed via ReadCache/WriteCache.

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_Cache
objects.role: the plugin; owns the configured max cache size and LRU tracker, creates the cache/cacheSize tables and triggers

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_Cache::LRUMap
objects.role: mutex-protected least-recently-used tracker keyed by name, backed by a list plus a map

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_Cache::LRUMap::Entry
objects.role: one tracked key, holding iterators into both the list and map for O(1) removal

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_Cache::initCacheSize
objects.role: parses a size string like '16GB' into a byte count, defaulting to 16GB

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_Cache::supportedRequestVerbs
objects.role: the verb set this plugin answers to (ReadCache, WriteCache)

objects.name: BedrockCacheCommand
objects.role: BedrockCommand implementing peek() (ReadCache) and process() (WriteCache)

objects.name: BedrockCacheCommand::plugin
objects.role: casts the base command's plugin pointer back to BedrockPlugin_Cache&

misfits.why: a fully generic string-keyed LRU tracker with no cache-plugin-specific logic, nested privately inside one plugin instead of being a reusable libstuff container

naming_quality.note: _maxCacheSize and _lruMap use the underscore-prefix convention for private members but are declared in the class's public: section with no private: reset, so they are actually public despite the naming

units.intent: A Bedrock plugin that registers zstd-dictionary-based compress()/decompress() SQLite user-defined functions, using dictionaries loaded once at startup from a dedicated DB table, plus equivalent static helpers for non-SQL callers.

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_Compression
objects.role: loads dictionaries at startup, creates the zstdDictionaries table, registers the SQLite UDFs, and exposes compress()/decompress(); has no BedrockCommand of its own

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_Compression::ZDictionaries
objects.role: pairs one dictionary ID's compiled ZSTD_CDict* and ZSTD_DDict*

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_Compression::_dictionaries
objects.role: map of dictionary ID to ZDictionaries, populated once at startup

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_Compression::COMPRESSION_LEVEL
objects.role: zstd level used for all dictionary-based compression

objects.name: sqliteCompress
objects.role: the compress(data, dictionaryID) SQLite UDF callback

objects.name: sqliteDecompress
objects.role: the decompress(data) SQLite UDF callback

units.intent: The catch-all Bedrock plugin that exposes raw SQL as a command: clients send a Query request and get back the result formatted per sqlite3-CLI-style flags or as JSON, with named bound parameters.

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_DB
objects.role: the plugin; recognizes Query requests and hands them to BedrockDBCommand

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_DB::Sqlite3QRFSpecWrapper
objects.role: move-only RAII wrapper owning the heap strings a sqlite3_qrf_spec's char pointers point into

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_DB::parseSQLite3Args
objects.role: parses sqlite3-CLI-style flags (-json, -csv, -separator, etc.) into a Sqlite3QRFSpecWrapper

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_DB::generateErrorContextMessage
objects.role: builds a two-line, caret-pointing error snippet mimicking the sqlite3 CLI's error display

objects.name: BedrockDBCommand
objects.role: BedrockCommand implementing peek()/process() for arbitrary read/write SQL with named bound parameters from sql-param-<name> headers

objects.name: BedrockDBCommand::SQLiteFormatAppend
objects.role: write callback registered with the QRF formatter to accumulate output

misfits.why: a generic sqlite3-CLI argument-parsing and error-formatting layer around libstuff/qrf.h's C struct, none of it specific to being a request-command plugin
misfits.suggested_home: libstuff/qrf.h or a new libstuff unit alongside it

name_fit.note: fits by convention as the original catch-all query plugin, though 'DB' alone doesn't convey that scope since every plugin touches the DB

naming_quality.note: Sqlite3QRFSpecWrapper's mixed casing matches the wrapped C API; depends on libstuff/SQliteParameter whose 'SQlite' capitalization is inconsistent with this codebase's usual 'SQLite'

units.intent: BedrockPlugin implementing a priority-ordered, SQLite-backed scheduled job queue (create/dequeue/update/finish/retry/fail/cancel/delete, parent-child job chains, calendar-style repeat schedules, and an operational job-name blacklist).

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_Jobs
objects.role: Plugin entry point: jobs-table schema/index DDL, supported verb set, and the in-memory crashed-job GLOB blacklist synced to peers on login

objects.name: BedrockJobsCommand
objects.role: BedrockCommand implementing peek/process for every Jobs verb, plus repeat-schedule and retry-after helpers

objects.name: scopedDisableNoopMode
objects.role: File-local RAII guard that suspends SQLite's update-noop mode while a Jobs command processes

objects.name: REPEAT_REANCHOR_THRESHOLD_SECONDS
objects.role: File-static cutoff below which a missed SCHEDULED repeat re-anchors to now instead of catching up serially

misfits.why: Hardcodes Expensify-specific job-name literals (manual/SmartScan*, www-prod/*, www-stag/*) as partial-index WHERE clauses inside an otherwise generic, reusable job-queue plugin
Generic SQLite-noop RAII guard with no Jobs-specific logic, named outside repo type-naming convention, defined locally instead of in a shared header where other plugins needing it could reuse it

misfits.item: BedrockPlugin_Jobs crashed-job blacklist (getCrashedBedrockJobPatterns, onNodeLogin, _crashedBedrockJobPatterns, CrashBedrockJob/ClearCrashedBedrockJobs verbs)
misfits.why: An operational kill-switch/ops-safety feature layered onto job scheduling; a distinct concern from job CRUD though tightly coupled to GetJob(s) peek/process

name_fit.note: Jobs.h/.cpp in plugins/ is exactly where a BedrockPlugin implementation belongs

location_fit.note: Fits the plugin directory; the Expensify-specific index literals inside it are the location complaint, not the file itself

naming_quality.note: Mostly _-prefixed private members and S-escaped 'safe*' SQL locals, but mockRequest/canEscalateImmediately skip the _ prefix used elsewhere, and scopedDisableNoopMode breaks the repo's type-naming casing

units.intent: A Bedrock plugin that speaks the MySQL wire protocol on its own TCP port, translating recognized client queries into internal Query commands (or answering them directly) so unmodified MySQL clients can talk to a Bedrock/SQLite node.

objects.name: MySQLUtils
objects.role: recognizes and picks apart specific client query shapes (VERSION(), CONNECTION_ID(), information_schema.*, SHOW KEYS FROM, foreign-key introspection) for rewriting into SQLite equivalents

objects.name: MySQLPacket
objects.role: encodes/decodes MySQL wire-protocol packet framing; builds handshake, OK, ERR, and query-response packets

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_MySQL
objects.role: the plugin; owns the MySQL-protocol port and translates between MySQL wire format and internal Query commands

objects.name: MYSQL_NUM_VARIABLES
objects.role: element count of g_MySQLVariables

objects.name: g_MySQLVariables
objects.role: table of fake MySQL server variables returned for SHOW VARIABLES / @@var

misfits.why: ~300-row hardcoded table of fake AWS-RDS MySQL server variables/values; pure static data embedded in the plugin's header/cpp rather than an external data file, dominating the file's line count

naming_quality.note: consistent BedrockPlugin_<Name>/g_ conventions; mysqlVersion/MYSQL_NUM_VARIABLES/g_MySQLVariables mix three naming registers but each is correct for its category
